annotations.text:
PLAYER, UNDER 18 — the full Phase 1 flow.

1 · The front door. 2 · Player door and date of birth. 3 · Build the CV — this is where the numbers are entered. 4 · Choose which of them show. 5 · Clips, ten free, no paid surface anywhere near this account. 6 · Give us a parent to ask. 7 · The wait. 8 · The parent approves (page 5). 9 · The CV goes live. 10 · Find a trial. 11 · Send the CV, or 12 · register interest — the guardian dispatches either one. 13 · Where the CV is. 14 · An edit goes back to the guardian before it republishes (D-119).

Browse sits BEFORE both outbound doors: those screens open pre-targeted at a club, and nothing else chooses one.

D-103 — CALLED BY BUZ 27 Aug.

Building before approval means the pending record holds a photo, club, positions, stats and clip links before any adult consented — which D-17 and doc 14 A17 currently forbid.

Approved on four conditions: unreachable by every query, rendered only to the child and the approving guardian, purges at 14 days, and the approval request shows the parent what the child actually built.

Build precondition: John reviews the widened pending record and updates the PIA first.

⚠ NATE'S PAGE IS NOW TWO TILES.

Removing minutes leaves the goalkeeper set as apps and clean sheets. Under the never-zero rule, a keeper who hasn't kept a clean sheet yet renders ONE number.

Nate exists to prove a keeper's page doesn't look empty. Look at him properly before signing this off — if it fails the test, the fix is giving GK a third number back, never relaxing never-zero.

WHAT THE SHARE BUTTON PRODUCES — and the parent approves it (BUZ, 27 Aug).

Screen 15 is where a player picks a shape. These three are the output, in three sizes for three places: a story, a square, and a landscape card. He posts them wherever he already is — Instagram, Snap, a group chat. Pitch does not post anything.

UNDER 18, THE GUARDIAN APPROVES EACH CARD BEFORE IT CAN LEAVE (page 5, screen 13). Not the share button, the card itself — she sees the exact image. Each card separately; approving one does not approve the next.

D-89 strips the under-18 card to first name, surname initial, positions, number and stats. No surname, no club, no age group, no region, no school, no face — and NO URL THAT RESOLVES TO THE RECORD.

So the arrival path is: a teammate sees the card, reads the word Pitch, and comes and finds us. That extra step is the price of the card being safe, and it is worth paying.

The honest limit, and it is on the parent's screen in those words: once she approves it, it is an image on his phone and nobody can take it back.

PLAYER, 18+ — the same spine with the guardian removed, and its own fixture throughout.

1 · Landing. 2 · Sign up, no approval step. 3 · Build — Nate at 18, senior club. 4 · Choose the numbers — he turns goals and assists off and ships two tiles. 5 · Highlights, three free with locked Pro rows. 6 · The profile. 7 · Pitch Pro. 8 · Trials — senior fixtures, not U13–U16. 9 · Send, no guardian confirmation. 10 · Share card, full detail.

What changes at 18: no parent-approved badge, full name and club on the card, a direct send, PDF export, the live link shown openly, and paid surfaces become visible for the first time.

11 · Register interest — the same screen as page 1 with the guardian step removed.

PITCH PRO — WANTED, NOT SOLD (D-104, called 27 Aug).

Payments do not ship in Phase 1. Pro opens in DECEMBER, alongside club search. So there is no checkout, and the button says "tell me when Pro opens", never "upgrade".

The want gets built properly: locked rows render legibly so a viewer sees exactly what is behind the door, the price is stamped "opens December", and one tap captures intent — no card, nothing charged.

The commercial point: three months from 14 Sep to December produce a warm list of named adults who have already said they want it. That is Pro's opening day rather than a cold start.

Don't merge this with D-87: 1 November is CLUB revenue, invoiced by bank transfer. Consumer Pro is December. Two dates, two customers.

MOVING PRO TO DECEMBER FIXED THE THINNESS.

At a November open, Pro was unlimited clips plus a PDF export — $79 for two things. Opening in December means it ships alongside club search, so clubs asking a player for their CV becomes a third Pro feature on day one.

The offer now stands up on its own.

The hard boundary that none of the anticipation touches: NO premium, price, upgrade, locked row or intent capture appears on any under-18 account, anywhere (D-82, D-88).

Compare Highlights18 here with Highlights on page 1 — same screen, and the minor's version is clean. A child cannot buy, so a child is never shown a door they cannot open. Anticipation is an adult surface.

These two are pre-launch and edge-case, not part of the running journey: the Australian waitlist from the tease window, and the overseas "bench" that non-AU visitors land on because accounts are Australia-only at launch.

COACH — complete, and the shortest journey in Phase 1.

1 · Landing. 2 · Sign up, Coach door. 3 · Build the CV — roles and clubs, badges, how you want to play, and the verification handshake. 4 · The finished CV, with a stable public link and PDF export.

There is no send screen here and there should not be. Under D-100 the coach COPIES their link and pastes it wherever they already talk to people — a club for a job, a parents' group chat to recruit. Pitch never sends it for them and never hands them a player's or family's contact details. The affordance is a copy button on the CV; that is the entire feature.

CLUB / TECHNICAL DIRECTOR — renumbered 27 Aug after the Interest Register landed.

1 · Landing. 2 · Sign up, Club door. 3 · Claim the page — it already exists, built from the club's public notices. 4 · Free, or the Interest Register — the plan choice, at claim time. 5 · The club page. 6 · Post a trial. 7 · The register itself. 8 · One entry, opened. 9 · What a family's revoked link shows the club.

The free email path is untouched and still the default: a sent CV arrives as an ordinary email with a link in it, and a technical director who ignores Pitch entirely still gets the CVs.

THIS REPLACES THE 'NO CLUB INBOX IN PHASE 1' NOTE — D-108 moved the register INTO Phase 1 as the paid tier.

Free club: claim the page, post trial notices, receive CVs by email. A technical director who ignores Pitch entirely still gets the CVs, in the inbox he already reads. That path did not go away.

Paid club: the register. $49 a month cancel any time, or $299 up front (D-109). Screen 4 is where that choice is made, at claim time, before the club has done anything else

THE STATUSES ARE THE PART TO READ. New, shortlisted, invited — three states, club-side only, and no fourth. There is no reject button and there is not meant to be one: a register isn't a queue you clear, and the keeper you have no room for in September is still on the list in March. That is what dissolved the declined-state problem rather than solving it.

An invitation is a real contact with a child and routes through the guardian, exactly like everything else (page 5).

Search is still December (D-107). In Phase 1 the player still finds the club — the register changes what happens after they find it, not who does the finding.

PARENT — the seat that holds every control we advertise. Now complete.

1 · Landing. 2 · An SMS and an email arrive asking them to approve (copy written, doc 15 §1–2 — no screen needed). 3 · Approve the page their child actually built (D-103). 4 · Your family — what needs you, and every child on one screen. 5 · The controls for an under-16: the link and its expiry, which clubs hold it, pause, replace, the consent record, delete. 6 · The same screen at 16–17, carrying the two switches that were previously promised with nowhere to press them. 7 · A send request: check the address, press send.

Screens 4, 5 and 6 close the biggest promise-without-a-screen in the project. Every line on the parent landing page — 'you hold the keys', 'one tap deletes it', 'nothing exists until you say so' — now resolves somewhere.

8 · Confirm an interest registration — the guardian reads the child's own words before they leave (D-108).

SCREEN 3 REPLACED AN EARLIER APPROVAL SCREEN, NOW REMOVED FROM THE DECK.

The signed version asked a parent to approve an abstraction. This one shows them the page their child actually made — the photo, the numbers, the sentence he wrote about himself, the clips — and asks them to approve THAT, with an 'open the full page' link and a 'not yet, I want to talk to him first' beside the approve.

D-103, called 27 Aug. John reviews the widened pending record before it is built.

SCREEN 6 CLOSES A PLAYER GAP TOO.

Nate's CV carries a badge reading 'Verified clubs can find me' and until now there was nowhere on earth to turn that off. D-22 makes it a launch control with a guardian override — it is here.

The precision worth holding: there is NO approval gate at sixteen. A 16–17 account cannot go active without a guardian contact, and that guardian keeps visibility, the discovery switch and the send off-switch — but the player is live and acts for themselves.

The screen also carries the 18th-birthday transition: access ends by itself, and giving it back is the player's choice alone.

CHOOSING THE NUMBERS (D-105).

STAT_SETS stops being the renderer and becomes the pre-selection — a keeper opens with clean sheets ticked, a striker with goals and assists. The football intelligence is kept, it just stops being binding.

ALL FOUR are choosable including appearances — your call, overruling me. My argument was that apps is the denominator that makes the rest legible; yours was that it is the player's record and we shouldn't bolt one hand to the wheel. Yours is the better principle.

Deniz has clean sheets switched on with no number behind it — that is the never-zero rule doing its second job. Choice selects, data decides, and clean sheets is not in the preview strip.

The keeper's version is on page 2: Nate turns goals and assists OFF entirely and ships a two-tile CV on purpose.

D-106 — anything outside Phase 1 is shown as COMING, never hidden and never live.

One chip, one wording: COMING DECEMBER where we have a date, COMING SOON where we honestly don't. Marked is the only honest third option — hidden builds no anticipation and reappears as a surprise; live-looking-but-dead costs trust on first contact.

The exception: no 'coming' chip for a PAID feature on any under-18 account.

And confirmed: no social-networking layer in Phase 1 and none implied anywhere. No feed, no follow, no connections, no likes, no comments, no in-product messaging. Sharing a card to Instagram is distribution, not a network.

D-93 IS ENFORCED AT THE CLAIM, NOT AFTER IT.

The claim screen makes the person say which role they hold, and prints the consequence next to each option: a club administrator NEVER reads a player's development record, by any route. The volunteer made an admin to send invoices cannot read a child's notes — and now they are told that at the moment they sign up rather than discovering it later.

Claiming and VERIFICATION are deliberately separate. Claiming gets the page and trial notices. Verification is a human checking the club against Football Victoria's register, and it is what unlocks anything to do with players from December.

THE TRIAL NOTICE CARRIES POSITIONS WANTED — and that is the part that earns its keep.

"Goalkeepers wanted" is the most common notice in Australian community football, and it is the field that turns a noticeboard into a match. A keeper scanning the board sees this listing first.

Competition gender lives on the SQUAD and the notice, never on a person (D-68). The listing carries added-on and last-checked stamps and takes itself down the day after the trial — a stale listing costs a family a Sunday morning.

THE VERIFICATION HANDSHAKE IS THE PART TO READ (D-98).

The coach does not enter a check number — the screen says so plainly: "Don't send us the number, we don't store it and there's nowhere to put it." The CLUB confirms the coach holds a current check, and all that ever exists in the system is a boolean.

That is what makes the build indifferent to how the NSW question lands. Whether we may hold a number, display a state or verify anything ourselves becomes a question about a field and about who attests — never about the permission model.

The CV publishes without verification. Verification is what unlocks anything to do with players, and it is free on every tier.

TWO LINK TYPES, DELIBERATELY UNALIKE.

The coach's link is STABLE and PUBLIC — a professional artefact that belongs on an email signature. The player's link is TOKENISED and EXPIRING, because it points at a child.

Opposite requirements, and doc 14 §J39 asserts they share no implementation: the coach route does not import the token resolver, the coach table has no expiry column, and no function is called by both. One shared resolver would break the safer of the two.

THE INTEREST REGISTER, UNDER 18 (D-108).

Screen 11 is the second door off the trials board. Some clubs take your interest inside Pitch; the rest read a CV in their inbox the way they always have, which is screen 10. The board tells you which, on the listing itself.

What actually leaves: a link to the live CV, the squad, where he'd play, and one line of his own words. No file, no copy, no date of birth, no contact details. Under 16 the child composes and the GUARDIAN reads the free-text line before it goes anywhere — that free text is the only place a child types into something a stranger reads, so an adult sits in front of it by design.

Screen 12 is the part the rename bought us. There is no result on it, because a register isn't a queue: no pending, no shortlisted, no declined. The words application, declined, rejected and unsuccessful are banned from the product (D-108 extends D-85).

SAME REGISTER AT 18+ — one screen, not two.

Nate composes and sends it himself. The only other difference is what the club can do with it: an adult's entry carries a reply address, a child's never does.

Riverside FC is the paid club throughout this deck, so it takes interest in-app. Northern United is on the free tier and still gets CVs by email — the two tiers sit next to each other on the board on purpose.

THERE IS NO INTEREST REGISTER SCREEN IN THE COACH JOURNEY, AND THAT IS THE DECISION.

A register belongs to a CLUB, not to a person. Giving a coach a personal list of players who are interested in him is the exact affordance D-100 exists to prevent — Pitch never hands a coach a route to a player or a family.

What a coach gets is the club's register, through the club's seat, under the club's permissions (D-93): a verified coach sees the squads he coaches, and a club administrator sees none of it.

The coach journey is therefore unchanged by D-108. Worth saying out loud rather than leaving as an absence someone tries to fill later.

PRICING ON SCREEN 4 (D-109).

The plan and the feature share one name: the Interest Register. "Club Pro" was called and reverted on 27 Aug — the register name is what makes an entry not an application, and D-108 depends on it being the word a club reads too, not just the word a player reads.

Monthly is the anchor and the annual is the price we want, so the saving is shown as a dollar figure — Save $289 — not a percentage. Trials are seasonal, so a club could pay $49 for three months and walk; the year-round framing of a REGISTER is what makes $299 the sensible line rather than a discount we hope they take.

Instrument is a CARD, through Stripe hosted Checkout (D-112, BUZ 27 Aug — supersedes D-87's invoice path, which is gone). Subscription state stays one flag on the club record, written only by webhook; the permission check reads that flag and nothing else.

D-113 is the guard rail: if the permission matrix is not green Wed 9 Sep, STRIPE is what gets cut, not the launch date and not the gate. The Founding XI pay nothing at launch and the first real club money is not due until 1 November, so holding that line costs nothing.

The line that must not be cut: paying buys organisation, never child protection. Both tiers use the same guardian-approved profile and the same revocable link (D-82).

SCREEN 8 IS SCREEN 7 WITH ONE THING ADDED — the parent reads what the child wrote.

The CV send only asks a guardian to check an ADDRESS. An interest registration carries a free-text line the child typed, so the guardian screen shows that line in full, with an edit beside it, before anything leaves.

There is no email address to check on this one: it lands in the club's register inside Pitch, not in an inbox. The guardian keeps the same two controls afterwards — take him off the register, and the entry and the link both go.

Screen 5 (the under-16 controls) now separates the two: Northern United was emailed a CV, Kingsway Rovers hold a register entry, and only the second one has a 'take him off' beside it.
